gaps.sentence: The play ___ when we reached the theatre, so we missed the first scene.
gaps.hint: it started before we reached it
gaps.explanation: The starting happened before the past moment of arriving, so the past perfect fits: had already started.

gaps.hint: consist is a permanent state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Consist' is a state verb with no continuous form: consists.

gaps.sentence: I ___ her at a conference in 2019, but we did not start working together until last year.
gaps.hint: in 2019 pins a finished past time
gaps.explanation: 'In 2019' is a finished past time, so the past simple is required: met.

gaps.sentence: While I ___ the report yesterday, my laptop battery died.
gaps.hint: the battery died interrupted the writing
gaps.explanation: The dying battery interrupted the ongoing writing, so the past continuous fits: was writing.

gaps.sentence: She has bought the paint, so tomorrow she ___ the kitchen.
gaps.hint: an intention already decided before speaking
gaps.explanation: An intention decided before the moment of speaking uses 'be going to': is going to paint.

gaps.sentence: The moon ___ round the Earth roughly every 27 days.
gaps.hint: a timeless fact about the moon
gaps.explanation: Timeless facts take the present simple: goes.

gaps.sentence: My back hurts because I ___ the garden all afternoon.
gaps.hint: all afternoon explains the present pain
gaps.explanation: A recent continuous activity with a visible present result takes the present perfect continuous: have been digging.

gaps.sentence: When I got home, I realised I ___ my keys at the office.
gaps.explanation: 'Had left' — the leaving happened before the realising.
